doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

chapter: Old styles, big bands and rhythm sections
title: Born in the wrong era: his father's view and Pelote's musical tastes
summary: His father said the old days were the bad old days; Pelote's heart is in old big bands though he likes bop and beyond.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Did you ever think you were born in the wrong era?

Oh definitely. Oh damn was I born in the wrong era. Oh God was I born in the wrong era. I would have loved to have been a part of that. But like my father always said, he said, “Those weren’t the good old days, those were the bad old days.”
I just was, that was sort of — I wondered, is there a good old days. But why would he have said that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Because of the racial stuff that was going on at the time. He was very aware of that, and while he never sat down and talked about any individual instances or episodes that he encountered, he never really talked about those days in a nostalgic sense in any way, shape or form. He always said, “It’s better now. Things are better now.” So I guess —
And he would have said that about when, in the 60s?

I would say as late as the 1970s. And one of the biggest regrets, other than the fact that I lost my father, he died in ’72 I believe, was that he didn’t live long enough to see Barack Obama become president of the United States. Because he always used to tell me, “There’s no way in hell a black man is going to be president of the United States of America.” He would not have believed it. He would never have believed it. And I would have loved for him to have seen that. It’s like, “See, Pop, it did happen, Pop.” That would have been great. Yeah, but that’s it, you’re right. Musically speaking that’s where my heart really is. Now I love modern — I love everything bop and beyond, I’m a big Eric Dolphy fan for instance, I love Eric Dolphy. I love Coltrane. I just heard some Marty Ehrlich that I thought was fantastic. I mean so I like some out stuff, I dig Ornette, I dig Jim Lyons, but really my heart is in the old. I really love those old big bands and the swing guys. And that’s my thing man. In fact the charts that you’d see in our big band that are from that time, I was partly responsible for getting.
